title.narrative: Third Disaster Risk Management Development Policy Loan with a Cat DDO

description.narrative: The development objectives of the Third Disaster Risk Management Development Policy Loan in Colombia intend to strengthen the Government of Colombia's program to manage risk resulting from adverse natural events, including disease outbreaks. It supports additional reforms in three policy areas: (a) promoting the further development of disaster risk management (DRM) and climate change policies; (b) strengthening the country's fiscal resilience to disaster, climate and public health risks; and (c) promoting sectoral and subnational co-responsibility in DRM and climate change adaptation. The program will deepen policy reforms by: (a) promoting co-responsibility across sectors, territories and government levels and entities; and (b) expanding disaster risk financing at the national, subnational and sectoral levels, as a key component of contingent liability management and consequently of fiscal management. The operation will also define and develop public policy actions to address climate variability; mitigate climate change by controlling deforestation and promoting the sustainable use of forestry resources; and contribute to mainstreaming disaster and climate risk in the development and operation of multimodal transport and housing infrastructure. Critically, in the context of the COVID-19 crisis and other public health threats driven by climate change, the program supports the formulation of a new Ten-Year Public Health Plan, to be incorporated into disaster planning and informed by lessons learned during the pandemic.
To strengthen the Government of Colombia's program to manage risk resulting from adverse natural events, including disease outbreaks

comment.narrative: Achievement: Fully achieved (100% of target) The Ten-Year Public Health Plan was adopted and operationalized, embedding climate, disaster, and pandemic preparedness. title.narrative: 3.2. Number of disaster risk financing strategies approved by prioritized sectors, and their respective implementation plans formulated

comment.narrative: Achievement: Mostly achieved (50% of target) The DRF strategy for the transportation sector was approved through Resolution No. 47935 in November 2023. The DRF strategy for the agriculture sector is in its final stages of the approval process. In addition, the Environment sector formally requested support from MHCP for the development of a sectoral DRF strategy. However, due to time and funding constraints, the Bank is not providing direct technical assistance for the preparation of the Environment sector's DRF strategy, as it did for the transport and agriculture sectors. Instead, as part of the legacy activities under the DRFI technical assistance, the Bank has prepared a manual on the development of sectoral DRF strategies, which can be used by MHCP to guide the Environment sector in the preparation of its strategy.

title.narrative: 5. Percentage of approved territorial development plans incorporating disaster risk management that are published through technology platforms developed by IGAC

comment.narrative: Achievement: Mostly achieved (78% of target) This RI was relevant and measurable but highly dependent on municipal approval cycles. By end-2025, 338 of 1,103 POTs (31 percent) incorporated DRM and were published, short of the 40 percent target. The target was ambitious given the complexity of POT formulation and approval. Progress nonetheless represents a significant structural shift in territorial planning practices. These POTs are accessible via IGAC's platforms, including the Colombia OT platform. Nonetheless, challenges persist, such as incomplete DRM studies and the time-consuming and costly process of updating POTs. Although IGAC is strengthening access to cartographic information, compliance remains the responsibility of municipalities, which often lack financial resources and technical capacity.

title.narrative: 7.2. Number of subnational health entities reporting public health risk maps for dengue/malaria and climate adaptation & mitigation actions under prevention & control of vector-borne diseases program

Additionally, 36 management reports on vector-borne disease (ETV) programs have been completed. The “Voluntary Collaborators” strategy, involving approximately 2,000 participants, played a key role in supporting ETV control efforts.

title.narrative: 1.2. Percentage of national territory covered by subnational profiles strengthened through the incorporation of climate variability analytics

comment.narrative: Achievement: Exceeded (115% of target) This RI was highly relevant to the PDO, as territorial climate characterizations underpin risk-informed land-use planning and directly support downstream reforms (notably PA5). The indicator was clearly defined and measurable, drawing on IGAC technical documentation. By end-2025, 37.8 percent of national territory (40.8 million hectares, across 393 municipalities and two National Natural Parks) had been covered, exceeding the 33 percent target. The target was ambitious but realistic, and its overachievement reflects strong technical capacity and methodological innovation at IGAC. IGAC has also developed strategies to ensure that these characterizations remain updated and publicly accessible, thereby supporting the sustainability of the platform.

title.narrative: 1.1. Percentage increase in budget appropriation for the implementation of the Public Policy on Climate Variability

comment.narrative: Achievement: Exceeded (103% of target) This indicator was highly relevant, as increased budget allocation directly reflects government commitment and institutionalization of DRM and CCA policies. The RI was clearly defined, measurable, and supported by robust monitoring through SISCONPES and biannual reporting across 28 national entities. By end-2025, budget execution reached 72 percent of planned allocations, exceeding the 70 percent target. Although physical implementation lagged financial execution (64 percent), this reflects the multi-sectoral nature of the policy rather than weak commitment. The target was appropriately ambitious and was exceeded due to strong coordination and enforcement by the National Planning Department (DNP).

title.narrative: 2. Number of hectares affected by deforestation (compared to 2019 baseline)

comment.narrative: Achievement: Mostly achieved (78% of target, substantial progress despite external shocks) Significant progress was reported during the three-year duration of the project. In 2023, deforestation decreased to 79,256 ha, marking a 36 percent reduction from 2022 (123,517 ha) and a 50 percent decrease from the 2019 baseline (158,894). It was further reported that the 2021–2023-time frame represented the period with the lowest deforestation rates in 24 years. Although the numeric target (100,000 ha) was not fully met due to severe droughts and wildfires in 2024, which increased deforestation rates, and ongoing enforcement and coordination challenges, the magnitude of progress during the operation, especially given adverse climatic conditions, supports an assessment of substantial achievement.

title.narrative: 3.1. Number of disaster risk financing strategies approved by subnational entities, and their respective implementation plans formulated

comment.narrative: Achievement: Fully achieved (100% of target) The Disaster Risk Financing (DRF) strategy for Bogotá was approved in September 2022, and the strategy for Dosquebradas was approved in December 2023. Tolima's DRF strategy was initially prepared in 2022 but was subsequently updated and formally approved in 2025. Cali's DRF strategy was prepared and formally approved in 2025. Bogotá and Dosquebradas are already implementing their strategies, focusing on the quantification of disaster-related contingent liabilities to strengthen risk retention and transfer instruments. Cali is expected to begin implementation of its strategy with World Bank technical assistance, particularly on the quantification of contingent liabilities, following the same approach adopted by Bogotá and Dosquebradas.

title.narrative: 3.3. Percentage of households with female recipients participating in Families in Action program that are eligible to receive unconditional extraordinary or ordinary cash transfer following a disaster

comment.narrative: Achievement: Mostly achieved (96% of target) While the original Familias en Acción program was phased out in 2022 and replaced by Renta Ciudadana, eligibility for emergency transfers among women-headed households reached 96 percent, close to the 100 percent target. As the Renta Ciudadana program adopted the emergency hotline and continues to prioritize female-headed households for emergency cash transfers, the impact of the prior action remains unchanged, notwithstanding that Cat DDO III monitored progress solely against the original results indicator associated with the Familias en Acción program. The transition reduced formal comparability but did not negate substantive progress. It is also important to highlight that compliance with the target may not be fully accurate due to delays in updating the database to reflect changes in families initial conditions (such as deceased members), which could account for part of the remaining 4 percent gap.

As the Renta Ciudadana program adopted the emergency hotline and continues to prioritize female-headed households for emergency cash transfers, the impact of the prior action remains unchanged, notwithstanding that Cat DDO III monitored progress solely against the original results indicator associated with the Familias en Acción program. The transition reduced formal comparability but did not negate substantive progress. It is also important to highlight that compliance with the target may not be fully accurate due to delays in updating the database to reflect changes in families initial conditions (such as deceased members), which could account for part of the remaining 4 percent gap.

title.narrative: 4. Sovereign green bond issued, subject to market conditions, and results and impact report published

comment.narrative: Achievement: Exceeded (600% of target) The RI was clearly defined and measurable, though binary in nature (Yes/No target). By 2023–2024, Colombia issued COP 7.4 trillion in TES Verdes, with COP 117 billion (1.56 percent of total emissions in 2023–2024) allocated to DRM-related investments. While the indicator envisioned one green bond issuance, the Government issued six during the life of the project: three in 2021, and one each in 2022, 2023 and 2024. While the indicator did not capture the depth of impact, it was achieved as designed. Although the client was unwilling to commit to a quantitative target during project preparation, the indicator could have been designed to be more outcome-oriented rather than a simple Yes/No measure.

title.narrative: 6.1. Number of kilometers of non-concessioned national roads incorporating risk analysis and risk reduction actions in new construction, renovation and/or upgrading projects

comment.narrative: Achievement: Exceeded (194% of target) By end-2025, 2,257 km of roads incorporated risk analysis and mitigation measures, nearly doubling the target. Progress includes the rehabilitation of three bridges (Rosas–Cauca), interventions at 100 points along the Salamina–Magdalena corridor, slope stabilization works in Chaparral–Tolima, and hillside stabilization, hydraulic works, paving, and construction of a structural wall in Cali–Valle del Cauca. In addition, the methodology for quantitative risk analysis was applied to 508 kilometers of roads, including Cali–Buenaventura (128 km), Curos–Málaga (122 km), Popayán–Rio Mazamorras (67 km), Sogamoso–Aguazul (102 km), and Caño–Mojarras (89 km).
